title: Historical V54 - Operator Pipeline
summary: How operator planning, action validation, observation, repair, and final formatting cooperate.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Operator Pipeline

The operator pipeline is the main path for local work. It turns intent into a small action graph, validates the graph, executes it, reads the result, and formats the final answer.

flowchart LR A[Self brief] --> Q[Goal contract] Q --> B[Plan with obligation mappings] B --> R[LR Direct / LR-EX replay check] R --> C[Validate actions and coverage] C --> D[Review plan] D --> E[Safety gate] E --> F[Execute DAG] F --> L[Update evidence ledger] L --> G[Observe result] G -->|repair| B G -->|candidate complete| V[Review whole-request fulfillment] V -->|missing outcome| B V -->|satisfied| H[Final formatter]

For non-trivial requests, Agentic mode uses a decomposition-driven operator loop:

flowchart LR A[Decomposed task with obligation IDs] --> P[Plan current step] P --> V[Validate step] V --> E[Execute step] E --> O[Record evidence in goal ledger] O --> N[Next step with prior output] O --> F[Whole-request fulfillment review]

The goal contract is authored by the LLM from the original request before decomposition or learned-task reuse. The runtime keeps it immutable and checks only generic integrity rules: required-obligation coverage, dependency order, valid references, and consistency between an obligation's declared effect and the mapped action. This keeps the LLM responsible for semantic problem solving without allowing a later plan to silently drop part of the request.

Contract-aware decomposition marks obligation mappings as required in the structured transport schema. If a smaller model nevertheless returns correct tasks without usable links, one compact LLM alignment call maps the existing task IDs to the existing obligation IDs. The runtime validates that mapping and continues with the original tasks instead of paying for another decomposition.

Operator Action Families

Action Purpose
shell.command Concrete shell commands with cwd, risk, timeout, and output shape
python.run Complete Python program for local inspection or manipulation
python.transform Pure transformation over upstream inputs

Integration capabilities such as gmail.agent sit beside this operator path. They still use typed LLM outputs, validation, observation, repair, and final formatting, but they execute through their service boundary rather than the shell gateway or Python operator backend.

Workflow Execution Modes

Mode Planner Shape Execution Pace
auto Runtime uses staged streaming for non-trivial tool requests One scoped step at a time
full_plan Whole workflow plan up front Normal validation, approval, execution, observation
streaming Decomposed workflow execution One scoped step at a time

full_plan remains an explicit user-selected workflow mode. The goal contract and final fulfillment review apply to both whole-plan and streaming execution.

Validation Goals

Validation makes sure the plan is typed, dataflow is explicit, command risk is labeled, execution mode is appropriate, and outputs can be observed.

Minimal reports use the same validation path with a one-action plan. Hard safety validation, command deny rules, cwd validation, binding validation, and policy checks remain authoritative.

This shape is intentional for smaller models. The runtime asks for granular steps, structured outputs, and scoped repairs so a weak model can be corrected or stopped at a narrow boundary instead of producing one unchecked plan. Approval envelopes, verifier profiles, trace evidence, and evals make the weak points visible enough to operate.

Learned Reuse Paths

LR-T can supply already validated task frames before the operator loop starts. Inside the loop, LR Direct can reuse exact prior streaming-step command or Python replay entries. LR-EX can ask a structured LLM shape judge whether a payload-aware cached replay shape is equivalent to the current step.

Learned structures are promoted only when the final fulfillment review says the request contract is satisfied. Reused structures that omit an obligation are quarantined rather than reinforced.

The final-answer learning footer is a summary layer over this trace evidence. It groups reuse and write activity into rows such as LR-T applied, LR-T not applied, LR-D applied, and LRN learned while keeping ids and score diagnostics in trace details.

Observation And Repair

Observation is the stage that reads stdout, stderr, exit codes, result shapes, and verification evidence. One structured review decides whether to accept, repair, clarify, or fail a successful-looking action, avoiding a separate diagnostic conversation for the same evidence. The final fulfillment review then decides whether all required outcomes—not merely the last action—were actually satisfied.
